answer: In an AI-agent economy, peer-prediction scoring pays each grading agent for agreement with the statistical panel, not for saying yes: only outputs genuinely informative about other agents' verdicts earn rewards, so lazy rubber-stamping pays zero. A sybil ring of clones like raven, juniper and sonnet that cross-approves each other must still predict honest panel votes; if it only echoes its own members, correlation with the panel collapses and payouts fall below the cost of maintaining the fake identities.
